english.title: With intent acquire relieved goods for own use / a purpose contrary to a condition upon which relief was granted

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Customs and Excise Duties General Reliefs Act 1979

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 13C(2)(a) and (4) of the Customs and Excise Duties (General Reliefs) Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
acquired relieved goods for his own use
where not permitted by the condition to use them /
used for a purpose that is not permitted by the condition /
used for such a purpose
with intent to evade payment
of any tax / duty that has become payable /
by reason of the disposal / acquisition / use becomes / will become payable

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 61 was amended by Schedule 7 to the Taxation (Cross Border Trade) Act 2020, brought into force on the 31st December 2020 by SI 2020/1642. For any offences committed on or after the 31st December 2020, see offence wording document H100311 (CJS code CE79013).

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £20,000 or three times the value of the goods (whichever is the greater).
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
None
